evidence_quotes.quote: This paper examines the allocation of PENNVEST funds to small water systems in Pennsylvania.
this research determines the effect of size of the population served by the water system on its acquisition of aid from PENNVEST.

the infrequent rates of participation by very small systems in the PENNVEST program suggest that the program's extensive application procedure may counter any effort to address the small water system problem.

The linked PENNVEST and state inventory data allow for the two comparisons made in this study. The first compares the size of the water systems that applied to PENNVEST and the size distribution of water systems in Pennsylvania generally. The second contrasts the size of applicants who received aid with those that did not.
PA DEP will not release data on instances of SDWA violations — a proxy measure of need — for individual systems to protect the privacy of the communities involved.

criterion_notes.c1: Does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access; all units studied are existing community water systems (piping water to at least 15 connections or 25 residents) and the study examines utilities' access to financial capital (state construction loans and grants) for infrastructure rehabilitation and Safe Drinking Water Act compliance.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the paper discusses an administrative/institutional factor — the Pennsylvania Infrastructure Investment Authority (PENNVEST) public financing program, its one-year application review/expiration process, loan-repayment considerations, and U.S. EPA size classifications — although the sole independent variable empirically tested in the statistical analyses is water system population size rather than a legal or administrative rule. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification, intergovernmental capital grant/loan allocation to utilities and system population size do not constitute a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as customer eligibility screening, documentation/tenure requirements, user tariffs, enforcement/disconnection, or utility regulatory structure governing consumer access). Criterion 2 is therefore not met.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical analysis linking state inventory records from PA DEP (2,331 community water systems) and PENNVEST construction application records from 1988 to 1997 (509 applications from 384 systems; comparison sample n = 241 applications), analyzed with Pearson chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports only utility-level capital financing outcomes: (1) whether a community water system submitted a construction funding application to PENNVEST and (2) whether the applicant received a PENNVEST loan or grant award (funded vs. not-funded). Does not report any outcome measuring household or community water access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, user affordability, or exclusion (and PA DEP did not release system-level SDWA violation data).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (Pennsylvania community water systems and PENNVEST construction project applications), exposure (water system size measured by population served), outcome (PENNVEST application submission and funding receipt), and study design (quantitative cross-sectional analysis of administrative records) are clearly reported.

study_design: Quantitative cross-sectional administrative-data case study (Pearson chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests)
population_and_sample: Community water systems (CWS) in Pennsylvania (N = 2,331 CWS in combined PA DEP PADWIS and PENNVEST inventory; 384 CWS submitting 509 construction applications during 1988-1997; analytic sample of n = 241 project applications: 191 funded and 50 not funded)
exposure: Water system size (population served, categorized by U.S. EPA size classes and analyzed continuously) in applying to the PENNVEST state infrastructure loan and grant program
outcome: Application submission to PENNVEST and receipt of a PENNVEST construction loan or grant award (funded vs. not-funded application status)
rationale: Excluded (E04 - Wrong outcome; also fails c1 and c2). Although titled 'Who gets clean water?', this empirical study analyzes intergovernmental infrastructure capital aid allocation rather than household or community water service access. Its units of analysis are existing Pennsylvania community water systems, its tested exposure is system population size, and its sole empirical outcomes are whether utilities applied for and received state construction loans or grants from PENNVEST (funded vs. not-funded status), with no measure of water service access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, household affordability, or exclusion.
